had increased odds of ICU admission and in-hospital death compared with nonimmunocompromised patients
Immunocompromised patients accounted for 12.2% of all adult COVID-19 hospitalizations
Among unvaccinated patients, those who were immunocompromised had higher odds of ICU admission (aOR = 1.26) and death (aOR = 1.34)
Immunocompromised patients accounted for 12.2% of all adult COVID-19 hospitalizations
Compared with nonimmunocompromised patients, those with immunocompromise had a statistically significantly higher prevalence
Among immunocompromised patients, those who were vaccinated did not have statistically significantly different odds
ICU admission model among unvaccinated patients was adjusted for age, sex, site, variant predominant period
Data collected on sampled adults hospitalized during March 1, 2020–February 28, 2022
COVID-NET is a CDC-funded collaboration for population-based surveillance of laboratory-confirmed COVID-19–associated hospitalization

methods_quotes.q: Pearson’s chi-square tests were used to compare differences between immunocompromised and nonimmunocompromised patients
Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to assess associations between immunocompromise and both ICU admission and in-hospital death
Associations between each individual immunocompromising condition and death were assessed using multivariable analyses, adjusting only for age and sex
Statistical analyses used SAS (version 9.4; SAS Institute) survey procedures to account for sampling weights
Percentages were weighted to account for the probability of selection for sampled cases.
